4:2.sourceText: καὶ γάρ ἐσμεν εὐηγγελισμένοι καθάπερ κἀκεῖνοι· ἀλλ’ οὐκ ὠφέλησεν ὁ λόγος τῆς ἀκοῆς ἐκείνους μὴ συνκεκερασμένος τῇ πίστει τοῖς ἀκούσασιν.
4:2.targetText: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.

groups.note: The actual copula and evangelized participle form the passive periphrastic good-news predicate, rendered we ... received the good news across also. Its English receiving/good-news expansion retains the actual evangelizing predicate, not a separate Greek receive verb.

Greek and-those/them in the comparison refers to the earlier good-news recipients; BSB expresses that participant comparison as they did. Did is English support repeating the preceding received-good-news predicate, not an independently written Greek doing verb.
The Greek benefiting/profiting verb is expressed by the English nominal predicate was of ... value under its actual separate negation. No independently printed Greek value noun is asserted.

The actual message is also the understood content of the final hearing/comprehending phrase; English repeats that same message as it. Both mentions retain this one actual message noun, not an invented second source object.

Greek of hearing qualifies the message; BSB turns that genitive nominal modifier into the relative they heard. The complete hearing noun phrase supplies this verbalized modifier, without claiming a separately written Greek they pronoun.

N1904 has singular passive not being mixed/united, modifying the message, while BSB follows a plural hearer construction and gives active share. The actual association/mixing predicate remains linked to did share with its subject/voice difference explicit; since expresses its participial explanatory circumstance, and the unlike English subject is explained separately.

The Greek dative articular hearing phrase identifies those who heard; BSB recasts its participant relation as of those who with faith. The case/relationship wording difference is explicit, not a separate Greek of preposition.

The actual Greek hearing participle is rendered comprehended in BSB, interpreting hearing as understanding the message. The same written hearing head is retained without presenting it as a different Greek understanding lexeme.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness construction difference: N1904 has a singular nominative mixed/united participle referring to the message; BSB follows the plural hearer-sharing construction and explicitly supplies they as its subject. This different grammatical subject is not forced onto the singular source participle.
